title: UN Security Council adopts Resolution 2728 demanding Ramadan ceasefire in Gaza
body:
On 25 March 2024, the UN Security Council adopted Resolution 2728 by 14 votes in favour, none against and one abstention, by the United States. The resolution demanded an immediate ceasefire for Ramadan, leading to a lasting sustainable ceasefire, and the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and humanitarian access to them. It also stressed the urgent need to expand humanitarian aid into Gaza.

The text was tabled by the Council's 10 elected members, with Mozambique's ambassador Pero Afonso introducing it on their behalf. It followed a veto by China and Russia on 22 March of a US draft. A Russian amendment to restore the word permanent failed for lack of votes. Ramadan had begun on 11 March, and about 130 hostages were still held in Gaza, according to the UN.

The United States said it fully supported the objectives but abstained. Israel said the failure to condemn Hamas was a disgrace. Algeria said the bloodbath had gone on too long, the State of Palestine said it must be a turning point, and Yemen speaking for the Arab Group called it a first step toward a binding permanent ceasefire. China said it came too late for those who had already died. Guterres said failure to implement it would be unforgivable.
